transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-21 15:00 PDT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (Timberlane Head of Search), Nia Okafor (Timberlane ML Eng), Ben Cole (Timberlane CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Walkthrough of hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints. Discussed throughput, latency budgets, and security/compliance (SAML, KMS, retention). Agreed on pilot details and follow-ups.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account, with Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Mark Rivera: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to see the hosted flow.
[00:12] Priya Sharma: Hey! Quick agenda: run through embeddings endpoint, then reranker/candidate scoring, show console metrics and Optimize suggestions, and leave time for questions.
[00:21] Nia Okafor: That sounds good. We'll jump in. We're mostly interested in improving search precision on product lookup, reducing bad top-k results.
[00:28] Ben Cole: Also want clarity on data residency and what stays in your systems.
[00:33] Alex Mercer: Absolutely. We'll cover retention and K M S, what logs live in-hosted, and options for private deployment if needed later.

[00:45] Priya Sharma: Alright starting demo — I'm switching to the console. Heads up, audio clip — sorry navigating. (brief pause) Ok on screen is the embeddings API. You can post vectors, or call our /embeddings endpoint with text payload, we return a 1536-dim vector by default for the model variant we picked here.
[01:10] Mark Rivera: Quick Q — do you support multiple models for embeddings? We have different content types.
[01:14] Priya Sharma: Yes, you can select curated model variants in the catalog. There's a small-cost/fast variant and a higher-fidelity one. You can pin per-route at the API layer. We also show perf profiles — p50, p95 latencies.
[01:28] Nia Okafor: How about batching? Our traffic is bursty during release windows.
[01:33] Priya Sharma: The hosted runtime does continuous batching. For embeddings we also have bulk upload endpoints. You can configure a batching window in the Dedicated product, but hosted picks good defaults — we show batching efficiency in Optimize.

[01:50] Alex Mercer: We mentioned reranking earlier. Priya, can you switch to the rerank flow?
[01:53] Priya Sharma: Sure — reranker is a separate endpoint: you send candidate documents + query and it returns a score ordering and optional salience snippets. We demonstrated a sample pipeline in the repo link earlier.
[02:10] Mark Rivera: Do you do both retrieval and rerank or just rerank? We currently use an external vector DB.
[02:16] Priya Sharma: Good question — Redwood's hosted API expects you to provide candidates. We can do embeddings and return vectors, but we don't host a managed vector DB; customers plug in Milvus/FAISS/managed vector DBs. A fair few customers use hosted embeddings + their DB + Redwood reranker.
[02:33] Ben Cole: So the flow would be: query -> vector db top-k -> call Redwood rerank -> present top results, is that right?
[02:39] Priya Sharma: Exactly. And we support partial rerank where you only score top-50 candidates to save cost.

[02:55] Speaker 1: (inaudible) ... latency numbers?
[02:58] Priya Sharma: For the reranker, typical p50 is 40-80 ms for small sequence lengths on our n1 variants, p95 higher measured in our perf table. We'll send the perf profile. Latency scales with sequence length and sequence pair token count.
[03:16] Mark Rivera: We're aiming for sub-200ms end-to-end on average, that's including DB lookup. Any best practices?
[03:22] Priya Sharma: Yes. Use prefix caching for common queries, do a small candidate set, and tune the reranker model size vs cost. Optimize recommends quantization and batch sizes. Also colocate the vector DB queries near Redwood region to reduce network hop.

[03:40] Nia Okafor: About model drift — how do we catch quality regressions after rollout?
[03:45] Alex Mercer: We have eval hooks and ground-truth prompt sets. Redwood Optimize can run periodic evals on a test set and trigger alerts if MRR or NDCG drops. We also emit per-request scoring logs (sampled) into the console.
[03:59] Ben Cole: Is that tied to privacy — we don't want raw queries stored.
[04:03] Alex Mercer: By default hosted retains logs for 30 days, PII scrub is configurable; for stricter needs you can request private deployment or use dedicated capacity with controlled retention. Our security pack outlines retention and scrub rules.

[04:20] Mark Rivera: On the security side we need SOC2 + SAML for SSO and customer-managed K M S.
[04:25] Priya Sharma: We are SOC2 Type II. We support SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning. For hosted, we integrate with customer KMS via an HSM-backed key provider for encryption at rest on certain plans; otherwise we provide envelope encryption. We'll link the security pack.
[04:40] Nia Okafor: Any HIPAA or healthcare-specific compliance?
[04:43] Alex Mercer: We have customers in regulated sectors; for HIPAA workflows we recommend Private deployment. We'll share a summary of controls.

[04:58] Priya Sharma: Back to the demo — showing a quick live rerank example. I'm sending a query 'best replacement part for X-14 hinge' and five candidates. The API returns re-ordered list with scores and an explain-like snippet. You can also ask for token-level attention but that's more expensive.
[05:20] Mark Rivera: The snippet looks useful. How deterministic are scores across deployments? We need reproducibility for audits.
[05:27] Priya Sharma: You can pin model versions; we have deterministic runs at the same model+seed, though floating ops across hardware could cause tiny churn. For strict determinism consider dedicated reserved capacity with fixed runtime kernel selection.
[05:43] Ben Cole: Pricing — ballpark for 100k queries/day with rerank top-50?
[05:48] Alex Mercer: Roughly depends on tokens and model size. We'll calculate TCO in the spreadsheet, but hosted can be cheaper if you rely on smaller reranker variants and caching. Dedicated is better for consistent heavy loads. We'll send an example TCO.

[06:05] Nia Okafor: About integration, do you have SDKs for python and node?
[06:09] Priya Sharma: Yes, official SDKs and snippets in the sample repo. The notebook we share is python-based and shows vectorization + top-k call + rerank call.

[06:25] Mark Rivera: For pilot success metrics: we want +8% MRR on top-1 and 30% fewer manual re-routes in customer support. Timeline ideally within 2-3 weeks.
[06:36] Alex Mercer: That seems reasonable for a 2-week pilot with a synthetic load then real traffic. We'll define measurement hooks.

[06:50] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) Are there any limits on request size?
[06:55] Priya Sharma: Payload limits are documented — candidate list size default 200, can be raised with a plan. Token payloads per request also have limits; we'll link the doc.

[07:08] Nia Okafor: We have an internal vector DB (FAISS) deployed in GCP; can you recommend network topology?
[07:14] Priya Sharma: Best practice is deploy Redwood in same cloud region, then use private peering or VPC connectors to lower latency. For hosted customers we support VPC peering for Enterprise tiers. If latency matters, Dedicated or Private avoids public network hops.

[07:35] Ben Cole: Any concerns about vendor lock-in?
[07:38] Alex Mercer: We avoid locking — you own vectors and can switch model variants, export logs. Our API is model-agnostic: you bring your embeddings or use ours. The only sticky bit is rollouts and caching layers, but we have export tooling.

[07:55] Mark Rivera: Ok next — benchmarking. Can we run a small perf bench with our top 500 queries?
[07:59] Priya Sharma: Absolutely. For the pilot we recommend a perf run: 1) we run synthetic concurrency tests, 2) you run sample queries to measure end-to-end p95, and 3) we run replica tests with your vector db nearby. Priya: I'll run the perf harness with your logs.

[08:22] Alex Mercer: Quick note on cost controls: set rate limits and quotas per-key. We also have per-route budgets. Optimize suggestions can recommend when to quantize or switch to a smaller model to meet cost SLOs.

[08:37] Nia Okafor: Is quantization supported in hosted? Any quality regressions we should expect?
[08:42] Priya Sharma: We offer quantized model variants. Optimize will evaluate quality tradeoffs on your eval sets and give a recommended quantization level. Some domain-specific terms can degrade — we'll show sample diffs.

[09:00] Ben Cole: What's the onboarding time for pilot?
[09:03] Alex Mercer: We can start within a week. Typical tasks: security review, API key provisioning, sample corpus upload, perf run. For Enterprise SSO + peering there's an extra 2-3 weeks.

[09:18] Mark Rivera: Sounds good. Any blockers for us? We need security docs to show procurement.
[09:22] Alex Mercer: We'll send the security pack and SOC2 report. Also send a stub contract/term sheet for pilot.

[09:35] Priya Sharma: Demo wrap-up — console shows cost breakdown by route and token; here's the Optimize suggestion that told me to reduce rerank top-k to 50 for this workload, saving ~40% cost in model inference.

[09:49] Nia Okafor: Nice. A couple of nitpicks: we need deterministic scoring sampling for audits; also we'd like more visibility into intermediate embeddings.
[09:58] Priya Sharma: We can expose sampled embeddings in logs behind a flag; deterministic scoring we can discuss as a dedicated plan.

[10:12] Alex Mercer: Ok let's do a recap of next steps: I'll send pricing + security pack, Priya will push notebook and perf harness, Mark will share query corpus. We'll schedule pilot kickoff for the week of 2026-03-30.
[10:29] Mark Rivera: Great. Thanks both.
[10:31] Ben Cole: Thanks.
[10:33] Nia Okafor: Thanks all.
[10:35] Alex Mercer: Thank you — closing now.

--- End transcript (transcription may contain minor errors: 'KV cache' sometimes became 'KV cash', 'VPC' was read as 'V P C' in places).
